title: Long-term Outcomes Following Implantation of Nickel–Titanium (Nitinol) Microstents in Schlemm’s Canal: Correlation with Optical Coherence Tomography
summary:
In patients with glaucoma, surgery can help lower the pressure inside the eye. During this procedure, a very small metal implant is placed in the eye's natural fluid drainage pathway. After surgery, it is important to check whether the implant is correctly positioned and whether the drainage pathway remains open.

The aim of this study is to assess the position and condition of the implant using a special, non-contact imaging examination. We also want to investigate whether the characteristics of the implant visible in these images are related to eye pressure and the number of pressure-lowering eye drops required.

To achieve this, information collected during postoperative follow-up is evaluated. A special imaging device uses light to obtain detailed images of the front part of the eye. In addition, the area where fluid drains from the eye is examined using a special viewing lens and documented with photographs. No additional surgical procedures are performed as part of the study.

interventions.name:
monocentric, non-interventional observational study involving adult glaucoma patients who have undergone Hydrus® Microstent implantation in Schlemm's canal.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with glaucoma who have undergone Hydrus® Microstent implantation in Schlemm's canal.
-Postoperative follow-up at the Department of Ophthalmology, varisano Klinikum Frankfurt Höchst.
-Feasibility of gonioscopy and anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT).
-Ability to provide consent
Exclusion criteria:
Acute ocular inflammation.
Other diseases or corneal opacities that prevent adequate assessment of the imaging findings.
